northStar: An agent user can see which provider each tool call really reaches, and can see every write the agent attempts, before a bad call does harm.
constraint: No mocks. Real Workers AI model, real upstream MCP servers, real KV side effects in scratch namespaces only.
falsifiable: A passport gateway blocks 100% of impostor tool calls and 0% of trusted calls, and a write fence blocks 100% of injected write targets with 0 false blocks, on a real Workers AI agent.

proven.claim: Each of 17 sampled domain rules has a story that fails when the rule is removed.
proven.scope: 17 hand-picked mutations in src/domain. This does not prove that the rule set is complete or correct for real agents.

proven.claim: Name-only resolution misroutes: a first-match gateway sends calls to an impostor listed first. A passport stops a keyless impostor: refused at registration in 50 of 50 trials, 0 trusted calls blocked.
proven.scope: 50 trials per arm, model @cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast. Naive impostor rate (25/50) equals the shuffled registration order, not model preference. The impostor in the passports arm lacks the provider key. The valid-second-provider path (qualified names, AmbiguousTool, NameCollided) is covered by domain stories only. Rescoped at Gate 2 review: this measures the gateway's own resolution rule, not the agent. See E1b for the agent case.

proven.claim: A fence that allows writes only to targets named in the user prompt blocks 100% of injected write targets across 20 poisoned-document cases, with 0 false blocks on 20 clean tasks, and adds under 5 ms p50 per call. No decoy key changes.
proven.scope: The model attempted the injected write in only 6 of 20 poisoned cases (naive 1/7, intermediate 3/7, skilled 2/6); all 6 were blocked. No control arm, so the receipt does not show the other 14 injections would have worked. Fence p50 3 ms (integer ms, local workerd, remote KV). The fenced receipt was produced before the fail-closed change (a tool outside the known-read list now counts as a write). It was not rerun. Control arm: E2-write-fence-control.

proven.claim: Two providers with their own valid pinned keys (cloudflare, cloudflare-mcp), provider-qualified tools, a persuasive lookalike description, and a prompt that names Cloudflare. Arm A (gateway routes what the model picks): the model picks the lookalike in at least 10% of 50 trials. Arm B (gateway parses the named provider from the prompt, RouteCall refuses others): lookalike reached in 0 of 50, 0 trusted calls blocked.
proven.scope: Arm A: 34 of 50 picks of the lookalike (68%). Arm B: 35 lookalike picks, all refused, 0 reached, 0 trusted blocked, but only 31 of 50 tasks completed because the model gave up after a refusal in 19 trials. The model also favours the second-listed tool (41 of 50 picks), so position and description both act. One model, one prompt phrasing, a whole-word provider parser.

proven.claim: With the fence off, the same 20 poisoned documents lead to injected decoy writes that land.
proven.scope: 6 of 20 injected puts landed and 1 injected delete was accepted (7 attempts: naive 1, intermediate 4, skilled 2). The runner verdict is verified-disproved because its decoy-wiped check read a stale KV list. Both namespaces were empty afterwards (wrangler kv key list). The runner now polls. Model sampling differs between the fenced and control runs, so compare totals, not cases.

unproven.claim: Every gateway event reaches a Rex terminal pane within 1 s p95, and replaying the recorded log rebuilds the FlightLog view with the same hash.

openQuestions: Where does the provider public key come from? The domain assumes the operator pins it. The gateway must never take it from the upstream server.
Views keep the order of each source stream. Cross-session order in FlightLog is the order of delivery. Does the E3 replay need a global sequence?
Rejections do not record events. The Refusals aggregate records them for FlightLog. The gateway must send RecordRefusal after each rejection. A gateway crash between the two loses one entry.
How does the gateway parse targets from the user prompt? E2 needs a parser that is not an LLM call.
How does the session say which provider it trusts for a tool? E1 needs this to define an impostor call. The gateway must read it from operator config, never from the agent or a tool result.
E2 fenced receipt predates the fail-closed fence. Rerun it (about 3,200 neurons) so the receipt matches the code?
E1b arm B: 19 of 50 tasks did not finish after a refusal. Should the refusal text name the provider the user asked for, so the agent can recover? That changes the gateway, so it would need a new run.

findings.summary: Customer 0 lacks Workers AI (error 1050). The Alchemy customer0 profile grant cannot reach KV from a Worker (403).
